name: Diamond-Square Algorithm (Chunk-based Midpoint Displacement)
definition: A procedural world generation method that recursively subdivides a 2D grid into squares and diamonds, computing new cell values as the average of four surrounding cells plus a scaled random perturbation. It operates asynchronously on chunks to generate a continuous world model.
summary: This algorithm generates infinite terrain by recursively subdividing grids into squares and diamonds, distinguished by its asynchronous chunk-based processing and lazy evaluation strategy.
